name.en: Thanaka — A Ritual Worn with Care

teaser.zh: 在許多緬甸人的臉頰上，文化不是陳列品，而是一道每天都能看見的淡金色印記。
teaser.en: For many people in Myanmar, culture is not behind glass. It is a pale-gold trace worn on the cheeks.
teaser.my: သနပ်ခါးသည် မြန်မာတို့၏ နေ့စဉ်ဘဝနှင့် ဆက်စပ်နေသော ရိုးရာဓလေ့တစ်ခုဖြစ်သည်။

story.zh: 早晨的木盤上，幾滴水與一小段香木被慢慢磨成細緻的糊狀。有人塗成圓形，有人畫成葉片。Thanaka 不只是一種臉部用品，也是許多人熟悉的家庭日常。
story.en: On a grinding stone, a little water meets a piece of fragrant wood. The creamy paste becomes a circle, a sweep, or a leaf-shaped pattern on someone's cheek. Thanaka can be part of an ordinary morning—and a familiar memory of home.

context.zh: Thanaka（緬文：သနပ်ခါး）通常由特定樹木的木材或樹皮加水研磨成糊，用於臉部與皮膚。它與日常保養、審美習慣及文化認同相連；使用方式因家庭、地區及個人而異。
context.en: Thanaka (သနပ်ခါး) is a paste traditionally prepared by grinding suitable wood or bark with water on a stone. Used on the face and skin, it is associated with care, personal style and cultural memory. Practices vary by family, region and individual.

moments.zh: 先研磨，再塗抹：常見的圓形石盤是製作過程的重要工具。
moments.en: Grind, mix, apply: a round stone slab is often part of the preparation.

moments.zh: 臉上的圖案可以簡單，也可以很有創意。
moments.en: Patterns may be simple or decorative, depending on the wearer.

moments.zh: 它是生活中的文化習慣，不代表每位緬甸人都會天天使用。
moments.en: It is a living practice, not something every person in Myanmar wears every day.

note.zh: 文化不只有被保存的樣子，也有每天被使用的樣子。
note.en: Culture does not only live in museums. Sometimes, it is part of getting ready for the day.

sources.title: UNESCO — Thanakha cultural practice nomination for 2026 examination
